en: The Śrī Śatrughna Kavaca from within the illustrious Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa.
Agastya said:
Now, O Sutīkṣṇa, listen with reverence to the armor (kavaca) of Śatrughna, which bestows all desires, is beautiful, and increases true devotion to Rāma. (1)
Śatrughna, holding a bow and great quivers with excellent arrows,
stands beautifully by the side of the illustrious joy of the Raghus, positioned with humility;
while Rāma holds a most wonderful and excellent palm-leaf fan in his own hand.
I worship the great Vijayanta, who possesses a sun-like luster and stands in the assembly hall, fanning [the Lord]. || 2 ||
Of this Śrī Śatrughna Kavaca mantra, Agastya is the seer (ṛṣi),
Śrī Śatrughna is the deity (devatā),
and Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chanda).
"Sudarśana" is the seed-syllable (bīja).
"The delight of Kaikeyī" is the power (śakti).
"The younger brother of Śrī Bharata" is the pin (kīlaka).
"Bharatamantrī" is the weapon-mantra;
"Śrī Rāmadāsa" is the armor-mantra;
and "Lakṣmaṇāṃśaja" is the core mantra.
The application (viniyoga) is for the sake of pleasing Śrī Śatrughna and for the fulfillment of all desires of the mind.
Now, the finger-assignment (aṅgulīnyāsa):
Oṃ, salutation to Śatrughna with both thumbs;
Oṃ, salutation to Sudarśana with both index fingers.
Oṃ, salutation to the son of Kaikeyī with the two middle fingers;
Oṃ, salutation to the younger brother of Bharata with the two ring fingers;
Oṃ, salutation to the minister of Bharata with the two little fingers.
Oṃ, salutation to the venerable Rāmadāsa with both the palms and the backs of the hands.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other [limbs].
Oṃ, obeisance to Śatrughna, the heart; Oṃ, svāhā to Sudarśana, the head;
Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to Kaikeyīnandana, the tuft of hair.
Oṃ, to the younger brother of Bharata, the armor, hūṃ!
Oṃ, to the minister of Bharata, the three prostrations, vauṣaṭ!
Oṃ, to the servant of Śrī Rāma, the weapon, phaṭ!
Oṃ, born from the portion of Lakṣmaṇa—thus is the binding of the directions.
Now, meditation.
To the left of Rāma stood the gentle son of Kaikeyī, who was adorned with a crown and remained there with humility. || 1 ||
Resplendent with jeweled bracelets, armlets, and a forest garland,
he wears a girdle and earrings, along with a necklace of gems and beautiful anklets.
With devotion, she fanned her beloved husband with a fan—Rāma, the hero who fixed his gaze upon her, the increaser of Kaikeyī’s joy. || 3 ||
Two-armed, with lotus-like eyes, clad in divine yellow garments, possessing beautiful arms, handsome, dark as a rain cloud, and with a lovely face. || 4 ||
He lent an ear to Rāma’s words, wielding a sword that slays demons,
bearing an excellent bow and arrows, and holding a most noble quiver.
Seated in the assembly hall, he was charming, marked with a musk tilaka,
adorned with an ear-ornament upon his crown, and possessed a smiling countenance.
Born of the solar dynasty, possessing a divine form, the son of Daśaratha,
the god residing in Madhurā, the slayer of the asura Lavaṇa.
Having thus meditated upon Śatrughna, who has his gaze fixed on the feet of Rāma, within his heart,
this excellent and purifying armor (kavaca) should be recited for him.
The commencement of the Kavaca.
May Śatrughna protect me in the east, may Sudarśana protect me in the south, and may the delight of Kaikeyī always protect me in the west. || 1 ||

May the kinsman of Rāma protect us in the northeast; may the younger brother of Bharata protect us below; may he born of the solar dynasty protect us above; and may the son of Daśaratha protect us in the center. || 2 ||
May he who increases Kaikeyī’s joy protect me here from all sides;
may the dark-limbed one, the younger brother of the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa, protect my forehead for a long time.
May Sumukha always protect [me] between the eyebrows on this surface of the earth;
may the Lord of Śrutakīrti protect my eyes, and may Rāghava protect my cheeks. || 4 ||
May he with earrings on his ears protect my ears; may the one born of a royal lineage protect the tip of my nose;
may the youth protect my face; and may he of distinct syllables protect my speech. || 5 ||
May Vyātyūpaketu protect the tongue from Subāhu; may Pitā protect the twice-born; may Ramyacibuka protect the chin; and may Subhāṣaṇa protect the throat.
May the one of great splendor protect my shoulders; may he who fulfills the words of Rāghava protect my arms;
may the wearer of the bracelet protect my hands; and may the wielder of the sword protect my nails.
May the beloved of Rāma protect my belly; may the best of the Raghus protect my chest;
may he who is worshipped by the gods protect my sides; and may he of the beautiful countenance protect my back. || 8 ||
May the slayer of Rākṣasas protect my belly; may the one with beautiful eyes protect my navel; may Bharata’s minister protect my waist; and may the servant of Śrī Rāma protect my private parts.
May he whose mind is offered to Rāma protect my thighs; may he with a smiling face and bow in hand protect my knees here at all times. (10)
May Rāmamitra protect my shanks; may Sunūpura protect my ankles;
may Nṛpatipūjya protect my feet; and may Sudhārmika protect my intestines. || 11 ||
During the day he should be blind; at the time of eating, he should be honored with arrows;
while walking, he should be sweet-voiced like a cuckoo; and at all times, he should be the ender of salt.
Thus has this armor of Śatrughna been proclaimed by me to you;
those men who recite it shall be partakers of happiness.
This excellent armor of Śatrughna, which bestows auspiciousness and increases one's sons and grandsons, should be recited by men with devotion. (14)
Whatever desire a person may pray for through the recitation of this hymn, they shall certainly obtain it; this word of mine is the truth. (15)
One desiring a son shall obtain a son; one desiring wealth shall obtain wealth;
and one desiring their heart's desire shall attain it through recitation and other means—this is certain, for this armor of Śatrughna is indeed [the power] of the Earth. 16.
Therefore, this auspicious [text] should always be recited by men with devotion;
first, men should recite the auspicious armor (kavaca) of Māruti.
Thereafter, this auspicious armor (kavaca) of Śatrughna should be recited;
following that, the supreme armor of Bharata should be recited.
Thus ends the Śrī Śatrughna Kavaca within the Śrīmad Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki, which comprises one hundred crore verses of the life of Rāma, specifically in the Manohara Kāṇḍa.
